chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is acting as an Imam and begins with al-Ḥamd, and does not say Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. He said: It does not harm him, and there is no problem in that. The correct way regarding it is that we understand it as applying to the state of taqiyyah, not the state of choice; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.إِمَامًا: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under sensitive circumstances
key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: the normal state of free choice rather than compulsion
key_terms.الْحَمْدِ: Sūrat al-Ḥamd, the opening chapter recited in salat (prayer)
key_terms.بَأْسَ: objection, harm, or problem in legal terms
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah formula at the opening of the surah
key_terms.لَا يَضُرُّهُ: it does not invalidate or harm his prayer

ai.seo_question: Does an Imam's salat (prayer) remain valid if he omits بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ at the opening of al-Ḥamd?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on an Imam in salat (prayer) who begins with Sūrat al-Ḥamd without reciting Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm aloud. The report states that this does not invalidate the prayer, while indicating that such a ruling is to be understood in the context of taqiyyah rather than normal voluntary practice.
